lines: I remember being stitched back into myself. Your hands held the thread.
The cure left scars, but good leather can carry scars. So can I.
You helped pull me back when even my name felt far away.
I remember cold, hunger, and then your face cutting through the fog.
Being cured is not like waking from sleep. It is more like being returned piece by piece.
Some part of me still listens for that old <shake>groan</shake>. I hate that part.
You helped me back. I may not say it gracefully, but I know what that means.
The village feels different now. Brighter, maybe. Or maybe I can finally notice it again.
I owe you more than a discount and less than my whole life. I am still deciding where that lands.
Do not make a ceremony of it. Just know I remember.
Your face is worn into the memory, but the edges are rough.
I remember straps, shaking, and a second chance pulled tight.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.

I remember you, and I remember the tearing. Both are true.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
You walk in like trouble forgot to close the door behind it.
I have seen broken leather with better instincts than you.
Careful. The village has long memories and very little patience today.
You are not as frightening as you think. That may be the problem.
If foolishness made noise, you would drown out the bell.
Do not test me just because I am speaking in complete sentences.
Your confidence is <shake>louder</shake> than your sense.
